group: squamate reptiles: Indo-Australasian Varanus monitor lizards (Brennan et al. 2021 Syst Biol / Zenodo 5655818: 1,091 dorsal + 1,098 lateral crania across 80 taxa on calibrated Tree.tre; 33 dorsal LMs & 10 lateral LMs)

data.landmarks: Brennan IG, Lemmon AR, Lemmon EM, Portik DM, Weijola V, Welton L, Donnellan SC, Keogh JS 2021 Syst Biol / Zenodo 5655818 (`Head_shape_dorsal.csv` 33 2D dorsal head landmarks across 1,091 specimens; `Head_shape_lateral.csv` 10 2D lateral head landmarks across 1,098 specimens; 80 Varanus taxa).
data.phylogeny: Time-calibrated phylogeny `Tree.tre` (76 tips across Varanus + Shinisaurus outgroup; ~74 matched Varanus species).

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Tests the portfolio's squamate reptile entry (`squamates_meiri`) on a 1,091-specimen, 74-species time-calibrated radiation of monitor lizards (*Varanus*, from pygmy *V. sparnus* to giant *V. komodoensis*) digitized in both dorsal (33 LMs) and lateral (10 LMs) cranial views.

hypotheses.statement: Across the ~80 Varanus taxa, Thompson-7 captures > 55% of between-species Procrustes variance on both dorsal (33 LMs) and lateral (10 LMs) head views.
hypotheses.reasoning: Monitor lizard cranial evolution is dominated by snout elongation/broadening and cranial vault depth across dwarf rock-crevice vs giant terrestrial predators.

hypotheses.statement: Phylogenetic signal on `Tree.tre` is strong: Pagel's lambda > 0.7 (best model != White Noise) in Thompson-7 space for both dorsal and lateral head views.
hypotheses.reasoning: Subgenera (*Odatria*, *Varanus*, *Euprepiosaurus*, *Soterosaurus*) show strong clade-level cranial conservatism.

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction on `Tree.tre` beats the grand consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.85, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 1e-5) on dorsal head shape.
hypotheses.reasoning: Matches the 0.85 subjective prior registered for squamate reptiles in `thompson_dataset_portfolio.json`.

hypotheses.statement: Within-species intraspecific/ontogenetic cranial variation aligns more strongly with between-species divergence inside the 7-D Thompson subspace than in the orthogonal modular residual subspace (|cos theta|_T7 > |cos theta|_res) on the 33-LM dorsal head.
hypotheses.reasoning: Allometric snout lengthening within species channels interspecific cranial radiation along the primary Thompsonian elongation mode.
